outcome: Read to the end of the numbers article and used its source list to go to Web Summit's own pages; would cite Web Summit, not PrompTugal.news; would not answer the three questions but might take the 15 minutes because an AI-run newsroom tied to a vendor is a story in itself.

interview.q1: A tip sheet and agenda for Web Summit Lisbon, written and published by AI agents, with every number tagged to a URL and a date. The numbers article is genuinely useful as a crib sheet; the company pages are templates with a vendor's question bolted on.
interview.q2: A small team, Dinis Cruz as editor-in-chief plus Indi Gupte and a 'Vicky' or 'Vicky Wang', who also work on a product called RiskMandate, which is in the masthead as 'Powered by'. In practice the pages are made by agents with addresses like journalist@web-summit.vicky, and About says no human reviews a change before it goes live.
interview.q3: I trust the source list, not the site. The 'What this does not claim' section and the dated source URLs are better practice than most event coverage, and they let me check everything myself in minutes. But About admits the only check 'checks form, not truth', the editors work on the vendor whose framework is the editorial line, and I found small contradictions (no summit page vs two summit session links on Startup Portugal, two repository addresses, 'writing desks are next' under an article by a writing desk). So: a good map, not a source.
interview.q4: Tonight, open the Web Summit survey release of 22 October and the 'How we select our startups' page from the list and take my numbers from there. Ask the press office whether 70,000 this year against 71,386 last year means flat. Put Tuesday 10 Nov 12:00 (Startup Portugal masterclass) and Thursday 12 Nov 12:30, Stage 2 (Road 2 Web Summit winner) in my diary. Maybe a short item on AI-run newsrooms at the summit.
interview.q5: Maybe, but not to the questionnaire. My paper does not run AI agents in that sense, so 'what your agents can reach' does not fit us and reads like the vendor's discovery call. I might reply to take the 15 minutes as a reporter, because a newsroom run by AI agents and powered by a security vendor, at Web Summit, is itself a story, and Dinis Cruz signing it personally helps. Cite or link PrompTugal.news? I would not cite it for any fact; I would cite Web Summit, Lusa and the other primary sources it lists. I might link it once if I write about the site itself, described as 'run by AI agents, linked to RiskMandate'.
interview.q6: Put a human's name and a press contact on every article, with one line saying whether that person read it before it went live. That alone would move it from a crib sheet to something I could quote as 'PrompTugal.news reported'.

findings.finding: The 'What this does not claim' section answers a reporter's questions before they are asked: it separates 10,000 startups from 2,700 accepted, names the 2025 figures as Lusa and ApexBrasil, and says the full survey report was not read.
Every source in the numbers article is given as a full URL with the date read, so each figure can be checked at Web Summit's own page in minutes.
Each number in 'In short' carries its attribution in the sentence ('according to Web Summit', 'as reported by Lusa and ApexBrasil'), so it can be copied with its source attached.
The front page says plainly 'independent of Web Summit, not of RiskMandate' and links the disclosure, so the conflict is visible before any article is read.
The company page gives two dated, located, sourced sessions (Tue 10 Nov 12:00 Masterclass 1; Thu 12 Nov 12:30 Stage 2 press conference) that work as story leads.

About states that a change 'goes live with no human review first' and the check 'checks form, not truth', which rules the site out as a citable source for a reporter; no article says whether a human read it.
There is no contact or press link in the footer or in About's eight headings, so a reporter cannot reach a human editor to check a fact or ask for a correction.
The Startup Portugal page says 'there is no summit page for it in the team's sources' after citing two websummit.com session URLs on the same page.
The header balance falls from '£5.00' to '£4.96' and then '£4.95' while reading, with no explanation on screen, which reads as being charged without consent.
The balance shows £4.98 on the company page and £5.00 on About after £4.95 on the article, so the meter is inconsistent across pages.
The reading box says 'read 20%' at the end of the article after scrolling through every section.

About says 'the writing desks are next' and the agent 'started on 4 November', while the site already carries articles by 'Vicky Wang's journalist desk'; the About page is stale relative to the content it describes.
About gives the source code as 'SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__Web-Summit' while the footer of the same page gives 'github.com/PrompTugal/PrompTugal__News__Website'.
One editor is 'Vicky' on the front page and About but 'Vicky Wang' in bylines and the footer, so her published name is unclear.
Bylines are machine addresses ('journalist-europe@web-summit.vicky, for Vicky Wang') with no plain statement of which human is accountable for each piece.
The last 'source' is 'From the curator's map: S5, desks/curator/README.md... left to S13', internal workflow that is not a source a reader can use.
The headline puts '10,000 startups' in large type while the body says the figure is not comparable to the 2,700 accepted; the headline sells harder than the body supports.

The 'flows' and Reach/Mandate/Gap template asks a public startup programme how AI agents act in 'its product', which does not fit the organisation and reads as the vendor's framework applied to everyone.
The relationship graph is too small to read at phone width, and the page says 'the role is not stated in our sources' while the graph shows Startup Portugal hosting a session.
The phone navigation shows only NOW, AGENDA and a cut-off NEWS; COMPANIES, PEOPLE, PORTUGAL and THE GRAPH appear only on desktop.
Reader pages show 'Admin', 'Control centre', 'Design review' and 'Page views: paused on this device', which make a news site look like a staging site.

Portugal links take their date from the URL ('the date in its address') and the 'companies we follow' chips include KPMG, MEO and AICEP under a Portuguese heading next to a count of 8 Portuguese startups.
